capital-temp-anomaly.name: Capital city temperature against normal
capital-temp-anomaly.method: POWER T2M, yearly mean minus 1991–2020 normal
capital-temp-anomaly.note: at the capital, not the whole country

cement-co2-share.name: Cement's share of fossil CO₂
cement-co2-share.note: process emissions from making cement, as a share of all fossil CO₂

coal-co2-share.name: Coal's share of fossil CO₂
coal-co2-share.note: coal emissions as a share of all fossil CO₂

flaring-co2-share.name: Flaring's share of fossil CO₂
flaring-co2-share.note: gas burned off at oil and gas wells, as a share of all fossil CO₂

lowest.name: St. Helena, Ascension & Tristan da Cunha

gas-co2-share.name: Gas's share of fossil CO₂
gas-co2-share.note: natural gas emissions as a share of all fossil CO₂

oil-co2-share.name: Oil's share of fossil CO₂
oil-co2-share.note: oil emissions as a share of all fossil CO₂

orbital-launches.name: Orbital launch attempts
orbital-launches.method: GCAT launch list, orbital and deep-space attempts by launching agency's country
orbital-launches.note: every attempt to reach orbit, failures included, counted for the launching agency's country

orbital-launches-site.name: Orbital launches from its launch sites
orbital-launches-site.method: GCAT launch list, orbital and deep-space attempts by the launch site's country
orbital-launches-site.note: every attempt to reach orbit from a site in the country, whoever launched it

satellites-launched.name: New satellites owned
satellites-launched.method: GCAT satcat and ecat, payloads by current owner and launch year
satellites-launched.note: payloads that reached orbit that year, counted for the country that owns them now

us-aqi-p90.name: 90th-percentile daily AQI
us-aqi-p90.note: the AQI that only the worst tenth of days exceeded

us-co-days.name: Days when carbon monoxide set the AQI
us-co-days.method: EPA days CO was the main pollutant / days with an AQI
us-co-days.note: the pollutant with the highest AQI that day

us-establishments.name: Business establishments
us-establishments.method: QCEW total covered, annual average establishments
us-establishments.note: workplaces covered by unemployment insurance, each location counted once

us-good-air-days.name: Days with good air
us-good-air-days.method: EPA good days / days with an AQI
us-good-air-days.note: AQI 50 or below, counties with a monitor reading at least 180 days

us-grid-co2.name: Carbon intensity of electricity generated
us-grid-co2.method: eGRID2024 state total output emission rate, CO₂e (STC2ERTA)
us-grid-co2.note: at the power plants in the state, combustion only; not the electricity used there

us-house-margin.name: House popular vote margin
us-house-margin.method: MEDSL House returns, regular general elections, (Republican − Democratic) / all votes
us-house-margin.note: all the state's House races added up; uncontested seats pull it toward the party that holds them

us-jobs.name: Jobs located here
us-jobs.method: QCEW total covered, annual average employment
us-jobs.note: by where the job is, not where the worker lives

us-labor-force.name: Labor force
us-labor-force.note: residents working or looking for work

us-max-aqi.name: Worst air day (highest AQI)
us-max-aqi.note: the single worst day; one wildfire or fireworks night can set it

us-median-aqi.name: Median daily AQI
us-median-aqi.note: the middle day of the year; 0–50 is good, 51–100 moderate

us-no2-days.name: Days when nitrogen dioxide set the AQI
us-no2-days.method: EPA days NO2 was the main pollutant / days with an AQI
us-no2-days.note: traffic and combustion; the pollutant with the highest AQI that day

us-ozone-days.name: Days when ozone set the AQI
us-ozone-days.method: EPA days ozone was the main pollutant / days with an AQI
us-ozone-days.note: the pollutant with the highest AQI that day

us-pm10-days.name: Days when coarse particles (PM10) set the AQI
us-pm10-days.method: EPA days PM10 was the main pollutant / days with an AQI
us-pm10-days.note: dust and other coarse particles; the pollutant with the highest AQI that day

us-pm25-days.name: Days when fine particles set the AQI
us-pm25-days.method: EPA days PM2.5 was the main pollutant / days with an AQI
us-pm25-days.note: the pollutant with the highest AQI that day

us-precip-share.name: Yearly precipitation, share of normal
us-precip-share.method: nClimDiv pcpn, sum of the 12 months / the 1991–2020 mean
us-precip-share.note: rain and melted snow over the year, against its 1991–2020 average

us-pres-margin.name: Presidential vote margin
us-pres-margin.method: MEDSL county returns, (Republican − Democratic) / all votes
us-pres-margin.note: Republican minus Democratic share of all presidential votes cast

us-temp-anomaly.name: Yearly temperature against normal
us-temp-anomaly.method: nClimDiv tavg, mean of the 12 months minus the 1991–2020 mean
us-temp-anomaly.note: the year's average temperature minus its 1991–2020 average

us-third-party.name: Third-party and write-in share
us-third-party.method: MEDSL county returns, votes for neither major-party candidate / all votes
us-third-party.note: every presidential vote not for the Democratic or Republican candidate

us-unemployment-rate.name: Unemployment rate
us-unemployment-rate.method: LAUS, annual average unemployed / annual average labor force, not seasonally adjusted
us-unemployment-rate.note: by where people live; 2025 averages 11 months, as BLS does, since October was not collected

us-unhealthy-days.name: Days with unhealthy air
us-unhealthy-days.method: EPA days unhealthy for sensitive groups or worse
us-unhealthy-days.note: AQI above 100, counties with a monitor reading at least 180 days

us-votes-cast.name: Votes cast for president
us-votes-cast.method: MEDSL county returns, total presidential votes
us-votes-cast.note: a count of votes, not turnout: there is no count of eligible voters here to divide by

us-weekly-wage.name: Average weekly wage
us-weekly-wage.method: QCEW total covered, annual average weekly wage
us-weekly-wage.note: jobs covered by unemployment insurance, before tax, not adjusted for inflation
